title: PID Feedback Control
text: A proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller continuously computes an error value e(t) as the difference between a desired setpoint and a measured process variable, then applies a correction u(t) = Kp*e(t) + Ki*integral(e) + Kd*(de/dt). The proportional term reacts to the present error, the integral term eliminates residual steady-state offset by accumulating past error, and the derivative term damps the response by anticipating where the error is heading.
mechanism_template: Given a measured quantity, a target setpoint, and delayed actuation, maintain the target via corrective feedback using PID control.

title: Reservoir Sampling
text: Reservoir sampling draws a uniform random sample of size k from a population of unknown size, seen only once, using O(k) memory. The first k items fill the reservoir. Each subsequent item i replaces a random slot with probability k/(i+1). This preserves uniform inclusion probability at every point.
mechanism_template: Given a stream of unknown length, maintain a k-sized uniform sample using O(k) memory.

title: SCAN / Elevator Servicing
text: The SCAN algorithm services pending requests along a 1-D line by sweeping in one direction, picking up every request in path, then reversing. This minimizes travel distance and avoids backtracking.
mechanism_template: Given requests on a 1-D line, minimize travel by sweeping monotonically then reversing.

title: Simulated Annealing
text: Simulated annealing escapes local optima by accepting worse configurations with probability exp(-delta/T), where T decreases over time. High T allows exploration; low T accepts only improvements.
mechanism_template: Given a combinatorial problem stuck in local optimum, search by accepting worse solutions with decreasing probability.
